TL;DR

First, set up all things that https://zenodo.org/records/11070973 require. 

Then, unzip this artifact, replace the original Makefile, and place Eq_Check/ in the same directory of Makefile. 

After that, all set-ups are done. 

Experiment can be executed by running: make run-<benchmark_name>, where <benchmark_name> is same as the coressponding C code.

metadata.title: Reproduction Package for ASE 2025 submission "Synthesis of Precise Error Conditions"
metadata.description:
Reproduction Package for the Paper “Synthesis of Precise Error Conditions”

Abstract

This artifact is a reproduction package for the paper “Synthesis of Precise Error Conditions” which has been submitted to ASE 2025.

It consists of all executables, input data and results required to reproduce the experiments. In particular it also contains the original results of the paper and a way to generate the plots in the paper from it.

We run the experiments using 8 cores and 31 GB of memory for at most 200 minutes (CPU time). In the artifact we reduce the limits to 4 cores and 8GB of memory. While the reduction of cores will only affect the results related to the Wall Time (RQ2, RQ3, RQ4), the reduced memory limit might lead to more out-of-memory exceptions in this artifact affecting all results.

A full reproduction of the experiments requires roughly 2 years of CPU time. For demonstration purposes, a subset of tasks has been selected which should take at most 1 day to complete and will likely finish sooner. To test that everything is working as intended, we provide a configuration that terminates within ~5 minutes.

The reproduction package can be found in Zenodo.

Contents

This artifact contains the following items:

  • README.md: This file.
  • benchmark-defs/*.xml.template: Templates to generate benchmark definition files for running the experiments using BenchExec.
  • benchmark-defs/set_tasks.py: Script to change the tasks to be run in the xml files.
  • benchmark-defs/tasks*.txt: Sets of tasks
    • benchmark-defs/tasks-all.txt: All tasks used to produce the results in the paper.
    • benchmark-defs/tasks-subset.txt: Subset of the tasks used in the paper.
    • benchmark-defs/tasks-one.txt: Two tasks used only for the smoke test of the Artifact.
  • data-analysis: Scripts and definitions to produce the CSV files used to generate the plots in the paper.
  • config.sh: Configs with parameters for BenchExec.
  • Makefile: Makefile to run the experiments.
  • results-paper: Raw results of the experiments presented in the paper.
  • License.txt: License information for the artifact.
  • sv-benchmarks: The SV-COMP25 benchmarks, without tasks and programs which were not used in the experiments in order to make the artifact smaller.
  • 2025-05-31_submission_ASE25.pdf: The paper as submitted to ASE25.
  • Tools
    • CPAchecker: CPAchecker version Removed for Anonimity in the folder cpachecker.
    • DescribErr: DescribErr version Removed for Anonimity
    • BenchExec: BenchExec version 3.29 in the folder benchexec.

This ReadMe contains the following sections to help the user to reproduce the experiments:

  • TL;DR: A quick guide to reproduce the experiments and analyze the data.
  • Environment: Describes the environment in which the artifact was tested and can be run.
  • Example from the paper: A short description on how to execute example presented in the paper
  • Experiments: Describes how to execute the experiments and generate the results.
  • Results: Describes where the results can be found and how to analyze them.
  • Known Issues: Describes known issues when executing the artifact.

IMPORTANT: Terms Soundness and Completeness in DescribErr

DescribErr internally uses the words overapproximating and underapproximating for sound and complete, respectively.

TL;DR

We tested the artifact inside the TACAS23 VM (Ubuntu 22.04) with username and password being tacas23. To run DescribErr on single examples, 4 cores and 8GB of RAM are sufficient (cf. Section ‘Example from the paper’).

  1. Extract the files in the provided ZIP archive to an arbitrary directory and open a terminal inside it.
  2. Setup the environment of the VM using ./setup_vm.sh (requires root and will reboot your system).
  3. Set the environment variables:
  • source config_clean_vm.sh: if full read/write access for all tools to /home is fine (recommended in the TACAS VM)
  • source config.sh: if you have a overlayfs in version 1.10 or newer installed
  1. Optional: Run DescribErr on the motivating example on the paper with make paper-example
  2. Choose one of the following sets of tasks to run
    • make setup-benchmark: Reproduce all results in our paper on your machine (takes about 2 years of CPU time, requires 8 cores and 31GB of RAM). We strongly discourage from running this inside the VM.
    • make setup-benchmark-vm: Reproduce all results in our paper on your machine (takes about 2 years of CPU time, requires 4 cores and 8GB of RAM; final results might differ because of reduced resources).
    • make setup-subset: Reproduce the results on a representative subset of our tasks (takes ~1 day and requires only 8 GB of RAM).
    • make setup-testing: Smoke test the VM and the setup (takes ~5 min and requires only 8 GB of RAM).
  3. Run make experiments to run the experiments for CPAchecker and DescribErr. If you do not want to re-run the experiments in the paper, but continue the pipeline using our results execute cp -r results-paper results.
  4. Run make process-results to generate the results as HTML tables, raw CSV and plots used in the paper. Find them here: results/output.

Environment

The easiest way to use this artifact is using the TACAS23 VM, copying the contents of the artifact to the VM, and setting it up by using ./setup_vm.sh inside the root directory of the artifact (i.e., setup_vm.sh is visible). This should work for any clean Ubuntu VM.

To run the artifact BenchExec, Python >= 3.8, and Java >= 17 are required. Additionally the python packages matplotlib==3.10.3, scipy==1.15.3, pandas==2.2.3, venny4py==1.0.3, pyyaml==6.0.2, and seaborn==0.13.2 are required to generate the plots. Script setup_vm.sh takes care of their installation. A restart of the system is required.

Inside a clean VM, please see the documentation of the respective tools for installation hints. A non-exhaustive list of required packages: * CPAchecker: Java 17 * DescribErr: Python 3.10

NOTE: We assume that all of the following commands are executed from inside the root directory of the artifact!

Example from the paper

The motivating example of the paper can be found under: describerr/examples/primefactors-example.c

To find the precise error condition x % -4 == 0 || (-128 < x && x <= 0) for it you can use the custom configuration ./describerr/examples/primefactors-config.yml. In the interest of time, we restrict the config to only consider == as relation operator and % as arithmetic operator. We also showcase the extensibility of DescribErr by running a parallel portfolio of the verifiers CPAchecker and CBMC as validator for this example. The following command line shows how to execute the motivating example from the shell:

./describerr/describ-err.py --program describerr/examples/primefactors-example.c ./describerr/examples/primefactors-config.yml

Please be aware that this may take up to 45 minutes.

DescribErr uses the word overapproximating in the logs if it was able to prove an error condition to be sound. Analogously, it uses the word underapproximating in the logs if it was able to prove an error condition to be complete.

Experiments

Setup

Run source config.sh (needs to be repeated every time a new shell is opened).

Benchmark Selection

Depending on your available resources you can select different sets of benchmarks to execute the tools on. You have the following options:

  • A quick test with two files, which can be useful to test that the artifact is behaving as intended. To select it use make setup-testing. Executing this benchmark set should take ~5 minutes.
  • A subset of the tasks used for the benchmarks in the paper. To select it use make setup-subset. Executing this benchmark set should take around 1 day.
  • The full benchmark set used in the experiments. To select it use make setup-benchmark to run it with the original resource limits of 31GB RAM and 8 cores (or make setup-benchmark-vm to run it with 4 cores and 8GB of RAM). Executing this benchmark set will take around 2 years of CPU Time.

Running the Experiments

To run all experiments sequentially execute make experiments. This is a make target encompassing the following experiments, each represented as a make target:

  • experiment-cpachecker-verification-svcomp25: Executes CPAchecker on the benchmarks selected using predicate analysis. This is the same analysis which DescribErr uses internally for validating the error conditions in our experiments.
  • experiment-describerr-template: Executes the template analysis of DescribErr.
  • experiment-describerr-template-daikon: Executes the template analysis of DescribErr boosted with the error condition candidates generated by DAIKON.
  • experiment-describerr-interval: Executes the interval analysis of DescribErr.
  • experiment-describerr-interval-daikon: Executes the interval analysis of DescribErr boosted with error condition candidates generated by DAIKON which are in the form of an interval.
  • experiment-describerr-counterexample: Executes the counterexample analysis of DescribErr.

All experiments are run using BenchExec in order to ensure reliable benchmarks.

After running make experiments for a minute, the output should look similar to this for experiment-cpachecker-verification-svcomp25:

Results

Generating the Results

Once you ran all experiments execute make process-results to generate the results as HTML tables, raw CSV and plots used in the paper. You will find them here: results/output.

Known Issues

Warnings

Overheating

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the CPU was throttled due to overheating. This affects the time measurements in the results, but should not happen when reproducing the results outside a VM.

2025-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - WARNING - CPU throttled itself during benchmarking due to overheating. Benchmark results are unreliable!

Overlayfs

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the home directory should be given as an overlay or hidden. Currently it is not possible to do neither of those inside the TACAS23 VM due to its old overlayfs and due to not knowing the path to the folder where the artifact is being executed.

2025-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - WARNING - Home directory in container should be /home/benchexec but this directory cannot be created due to directory mode of parent directory. It is recommended to use '--overlay-dir /home' or '--hidden-dir /home' and overwrite directory modes for subdirectories where necessary.

Resource Requirements

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the resource requirements are being ignored. This only means that the resource requirements regarding CPU model are being ignored, this has no effect on the benchmarking.

Errors

Overlay

When BenchExec tries to create an overlay mount while there is a shared folder mounted inside the VM, the following error may occur:

2025-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - ERROR - Failed to create overlay mount for /home/...: invalid argument ...

In this case, the shared folder should be unmounted and the experiments should be run again.

C Groups

If BenchExec is unable to use C groups to benchmark and you have already run ./setup_vm.sh then a restart of the VM will help make BenchExec work as intended.

metadata.title: Time-sensitive Importance Splitting (experimental reproduction package)
metadata.description:
Artifact to reproduce the experimental results presented in the article "Time-Sensitive Importance Splitting" by Gabriel Dengler, Carlos E. Budde, Laura Carnevali, and Arnd Hartmanns,  (submitted to QEST+FORMATS 2025).

The contents include all data and software (formal models, software tools, shell & Python scripts) used in the experimental evaluation presented in section 4 of the article. These contents are offered in two formats:

  • The minimal artifact ("experimental reproduction package"), as the time_sensitive_ISPLIT_artifact.tar.xz archive,
    • this requires users to set up their system to be able to reproduce experiments;
  • A standalone VM, as the time_sensitive_ISPLIT_artifact.ova appliance,
    • this can be directly loaded into VirtualBox for experimental reproduction.

Detailed instructions on how to reproduce the results of the artifact are available as READMEs here, and also bundled inside the artifact files.

metadata.title: Reproduction Package for CAV 2025 submission `Certification and Validation for Program Termination'
metadata.description:
Reproduction Package for the Paper “Certification and Validation for Program Termination”

Abstract

This artifact is a reproduction package for the paper “Certification and Validation for Program Termination” which has been submitted to CAV 2025.

It consists of all executables, input data and results required to reproduce the experiments. In particular it also contains the original results of the paper and a way to generate the macros and csv’s to generate the plots in the paper from it.

We run the experiments using 2 cores and 15 GiB of memory for at most 15 minutes (CPU time).

A full reproduction of the experiments requires roughly 40 days of CPU time. For demonstration purposes, a subset of tasks has been selected which should take at most 1 day to complete and will likely finish sooner. To test that everything is working as intended, we provide a configuration that terminates within ~10 minutes.

Contents

This artifact contains the following items:

  • README.md: This file.
  • benchmark-defs/*.xml.template: Templates to generate benchmark definition files for running the experiments using BenchExec.
  • benchmark-defs/set_tasks.py: Script to change the tasks to be run in the xml files.
  • tasks/*.xml: Sets of tasks
    • tasks/all.xml: All tasks used to produce the results in the paper.
    • tasks/subset.xml: Subset of the tasks used in the paper.
    • test/test.xml: One task used only for the smoke test of the Artifact.
  • data-analysis: Scripts and definitions to produce the CSV files used to generate the plots in the paper. Additionally they also generate the macros used to generate the tables in the paper.
  • benchmark-utils/*: Benchmarking utils
    • config.sh: File with parameters for BenchExec
    • check_configured.sh: File which checks that BenchExec is set up correctly
    • metaval++*: Configurations for MetaVal++ for benchmarking
  • Makefile: Makefile to run the experiments.
  • results-paper: Raw results of the experiments presented in the paper.
  • License.txt: License information for the artifact.
  • sv-benchmarks: The SV-COMP25 benchmarks.
  • Tools
    • CPAchecker: CPAchecker version 4.0 in the folder cpachecker.
    • UAuomizer: UAutomizer in its SV-COMP25 version in the folder uautomizer.
    • Goblint: Goblint in its SV-COMP25 version in the folder goblint.
    • TransVer: TransVer at commit 04003e in the folder transver using CPAchecker at commit 004e6a
    • MetaVal++ at commit aced09 in the folder metaval++ using TransVer in the commit given above, SV-Transformer Lib at commit 3494ef, FM-Weck at commit 835813 and CPAchecker and UAuomizer in their SV-COMP25 versions mentioned above.

This ReadMe contains the following sections to help the user to reproduce the experiments:

  • TL;DR: A quick guide to reproduce the experiments and analyze the data.
  • Environment: Describes the environment in which the artifact was tested and can be run.
  • Experiments: Describes how to execute the experiments and generate the results.
  • Results: Describes where the results can be found and how to analyze them.
  • Known Issues: Describes known issues when executing the artifact.

TL;DR

Before starting, if you are using a VM make sure to configure it to use at least 4 cores, at least 16GiB of RAM.

  1. Extract the files in the provided ZIP archive to an arbitrary directory and open a terminal inside it.
  2. Set the environment variables:
  • source benchmark-utils/config_vm.sh: if full read/write access for all tools to /home is fine
  • source benchmark-utils/config.sh: if you have a overlayfs in version 1.10 or newer installed
  1. Choose one of the following sets of tasks to run:
    • make setup-benchmark: Reproduce all results in our paper on your machine (takes about 30 days of CPU time, requires 2 cores and 16GiB of RAM). We strongly discourage from running this inside a VM.
    • make setup-subset: Reproduce the results on a representative subset of our tasks (takes ~1 day).
    • make setup-test: Smoke test the VM and the setup (takes ~5 min).
  2. Run make transform-programs: To transform all the programs from termination to reachability for the verification runs
  3. Run make verify-transformed to run the verification of the transformed programs to reachability for CPAchecker, UAUtomizer and Goblint.
  4. Run make process-witnesses to generate the directories from which the witnesses will be read from. This symlinks the witnesses into that directory.
  5. Run make transform-witnesses to transform the witnesses from reachability to termination.
  6. Run make metavalpp-validate-all to validate the termination witnesses using MetaVal++ with all its possible backends i.e. CPAchecker, UAutomizer and Goblint.
  7. Run make generate-tables to generate html tables for each verifier presenting the results. These tables contain most of the results presented in the paper.
  8. (Optional) Generate the macros and csv used to generate the plots and tables in the paper:
    1. Run pip install -r data-analysis/requirements.txt.
    2. Run make analyze-results in order to export macros and csv files into the directory data-analysis/results. These were used to generate the plots and tables in the paper.

Environment

To run the artifact BenchExec, Python >= 3.8 and Podman are required.

Inside a clean VM, please see the documentation of the respective tools for installation hints. A non-exhaustive list of required packages: * CPAchecker: Java 17 * UAutomizer: Java 21 * Goblint: libgmp-dev and libmpfr-dev

NOTE: We assume that all of the following commands are executed from inside the root directory of the artifact!

Experiments

Setup

Run source benchmark-utils/config.sh (needs to be repeated every time a new shell is opened).

Benchmark Selection

Depending on your available resources you can select different sets of benchmarks to execute the tools on. You have the following options:

  • A quick test with a single file, which can be useful to test that the artifact is behaving as intended. To select it use make setup-test. Executing this benchmark set should take ~5 minutes.
  • A subset of the tasks used for the benchmarks in the paper. To select it use make setup-subset. Executing this benchmark set should take around 1 day.
  • The full benchmark set used in the experiments. To select it use make setup-benchmark. Executing this benchmark set will take around 30 days of CPU Time.

Running the Experiments

To run all experiments multiple targets need to be executed one after the other. Each of them encompass multiple targets for the different verifiers and validator backends.

All experiments are run using BenchExec in order to ensure reliable benchmarks.

The following targets need to be extecuted using make in this order: 1. transform-programs: Transforms all the chosen termination benchmarks using TransVer into reachability benchmarks. The produced benchmarks will follow the same directory structure and can be found in the folder transformed-tasks. 2. verify-transformed: This executes the verifiers CPAchecker, UAutomizer and Goblint on the produced reachability tasks. It encompasses the targets cpachecker-verify-transformed, uautomizer-verify-transformed, goblint-verify-transformed which execute CPAchecker, UAutomizer and Goblint respectively. The results when executing this can be found in results. 3. process-witnesses: It encompasses the targets cpachecker-witnesses, uautomizer-witnesses, goblint-witnesses which produce a symlink for the witnesses produced by each of the verifiers into a folder called results/$VERIFIER-witnesses. 4. transform-witnesses: It encompasses the targets cpachecker-transform-witnesses, uautomizer-transform-witnesses, goblint-transform-witnesses which transforms the witnesses from reachability witnesses into the proposed format for termination witnesses i.e. using \prev. The transformed witnesses can be found in the folders results/$VERIFIER-transformed-witnesses. 5. metavalpp-validate-all: It encompasses the targets metavalpp-uautomizer-validate-uautomizer, metavalpp-cpachecker-validate-uautomizer, metavalpp-uautomizer-validate-cpachecker, metavalpp-cpachecker-validate-cpachecker, metavalpp-uautomizer-validate-goblint, metavalpp-cpachecker-validate-goblint which validate the termination witnesses produced by the second tool mentioned using MetaVal++ with the first tool mentioned as validator backend i.e. they are of the form metavalpp-$VALIDATOR-validate-$VERIFIER. The results of each of these runs are found in the folder results starting with the name of the target.

Results

Generating the Results

Once you ran all experiments execute make generate-tables to generate HTML tables which contain most of the information also presented in the plots and tables in the paper. The only information missing is the related to the invariants contained in the witness.

If you so desire you can also run make analyze-results which will generate all the macros and CSV’s which were used to generate the plots and tables in the paper.

Results from the Paper

The directory results-paper contains the raw data which we obtained from our experiments. If you want to anylze it, you can rename it into results and execute the previous step to generate the analyzed results.

Known Issues

Warnings

Overheating

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the CPU was throttled due to overheating. This affects the time measurements in the results, but should not happen when reproducing the results outside a VM.

2024-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - WARNING - CPU throttled itself during benchmarking due to overheating. Benchmark results are unreliable!

Overlayfs

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the home directory should be given as an overlay or hidden. Currently it is not possible to do neither of those inside the TACAS23 VM due to its old overlayfs and due to not knowing the path to the folder where the artifact is being executed.

2024-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - WARNING - Home directory in container should be /home/benchexec but this directory cannot be created due to directory mode of parent directory. It is recommended to use '--overlay-dir /home' or '--hidden-dir /home' and overwrite directory modes for subdirectories where necessary.

Resource Requirements

During the execution of the experiments, a warning may appear which tells us that the resource requirements are being ignored. This only means that the resource requirements regarding CPU model are being ignored, this has no effect on the benchmarking.

Errors

Overlay

When BenchExec tries to create an overlay mount while there is a shared folder mounted inside the VM, the following error may occur:

2024-XX-XX XX:XX:XX - ERROR - Failed to create overlay mount for /home/...: invalid argument ...

In this case, the shared folder should be unmounted and the experiments should be run again.

C Groups

If BenchExec is unable to use C groups to benchmark then a restart of the VM may help make BenchExec work as intended.

metadata.title: Reproduction Package: Does the Tool Matter? Exploring Some Causes of Threats to Validity in Mining Software Repositories
metadata.description:
Study

The study uses the two mining software repositories (MSR) tools Codeface and Kaiaulu to extract and analyse ten large software projects, quantitatively and qualitatively comparing results and derived data to better understand the causes and impact of uncertainties in MSR tools and analysis pipelines.

The study can be reproduced based on our GitHub repository or this reproduction package.

 

Reproduction package

Due to the size limit of 50 GB, we cannot provide the fully self-contained docker image.

Instead, we provide all compressed artefacts and our study environment in the docker image separately.

The additional_material.zip may be inspected ad-hoc and is structured as follows:

  • analysis/: This directory contains all necessary bash scripts to reproduce our analysis pipeline as presented in the paper.
  • data/: This directory contains the git repositories and the data extracted by the MSR tools Codeface and Kaiaulu.
  • docker/: This directory contains the entrypoint script for the docker container.
  • log/: This directory contains log files of the comparative analysis scripts.
  • plot/: This directory contains the plots from the paper and the source code to generate them in R.
  • results/: This directory contains all results of the comparative analysis as CSV files.
  • src/: This directory contains our comparative analysis scripts in Python.
  • tools/: This directory contains the MSR tools Codeface and Kaiaulu with the configurations and adjustments described in the paper.

 

Reproduction setup

1. Import the docker image using 

docker load -i docker-image.tar.gz

2. Run a container from the image using

docker run --name saner -d -t --user saner saner

3. Unzip the additional_material.zip and copy the "db.sql" folder manually using

docker cp [local-path]/data/db.sql saner:/home/saner/data

4. Log in to the container using

docker exec -it saner bash

5. Import the MySQL database (password "codeface") using 

mysql -u codeface -p codeface < /home/saner/data/db.sql

 

Reproducing the analysis

We provide a single script to run all analysis steps from cloning git repositories, analysis with Codeface and Kaiaulu to baseline data and developer network comparisons.

Executing all analysis steps sequentially can be very time-consuming (up to several weeks) and risky due to sporadic parallelisation or database errors.

For quickly evaluating our replication package, you can exclude subject projects from the project_list in the /home/saner/analysis/analysis.conf in your docker container. The above script will then only consider the defined subset of projects. However, be aware that our visualisations are not optimised for this scenario.

If you prefer to analyse the entire set of subject projects with more control, or if you experience any errors, please refer to the "Important Notes" section below.

6. Start the study analysis pipeline in your docker container:

bash /home/saner/analysis/analysis.sh

7. When the analysis runs completed sucessfully, you can inspect the results on localhost with:

docker cp saner:/home/saner/data .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/log .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/plot .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/results .

metadata.description:
Overview

Date: January 2025

This file describes  the reproduction package for the following publication:

Authors: Florian Diekert, Daniel Heyen, Frikk Nesje, Soheil Shayegh
Title: Do early warning signals of tipping points lead to better decisions?
Corresponding Author: Florian Diekert, florian.diekert@uni-a.de
Publication: Journal of The Royal Society Interface


Software requirements

We use Python with standard packages. Specifically, the following packages and functions are required:
numpy, pandas, scipy.optimize, astropy.convolution.convolve, matplotlib


Description of steps

Running main_script.py will complete the following steps: 

- Function "population_model": Runs the socio-ecological system as described in Supplementary Material S2. Output is a csv file. On a standard machine this step will take several hours. The resulting file has a size of approx. 450 MB.
 
- Function "sig_func": Takes the output from population_model as input and determines the signal functions as described in Supplementary Material S3.  

The remaining steps create figures in the main body as well as the supplementary material document. In all cases, the signal functions created in step 2 are the input and function "optim_fun" (from modulefile) is used to determine optimal management choices as described in Supplementary Material S4. 

The script creates the following figures (source file "figure_scripts.py")

- Figure 2
- Figure 3b
- Eight figures for the Box in S1 
- Extended Data Figure 1 a-d

- Extended Data Figure 3 a-b
- Extended Data Figure 4 a-c
- Extended Data Figure 5 a-b

metadata.title: Reproduction Package for FSE 2025 Submission `A Modular Program-Transformation Framework for Reducing Specifications to Reachability'
metadata.description:
This is the Artifact for the paper “A Modular Program-Transformation Framework for Reducing Specifications to Reachability” which has been submitted to FSE 2025.

The FSE article presents a program transformation framework with the goal of verifying different properties with of-the-shelf reachability analyzers. The transformations in a framework is based on instrumentation automata, inspired by the BLAST query language. In our initial study, we support three important concrete specifications for C programs: termination, no-overflow, and memory cleanup. This artifact can be used to reproduce the experiments presented in the paper. We demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our transformations by comparing verifiers that support the specifications natively with verifiers for reachability applied to the transformed programs. The results are very promising: Our transformations can extend existing verifiers to be effective on specifications that they do not support natively, and that the efficiency is often similar to verifiers that natively support the considered specifications.

The artifact consists of Makefile that can be used to download all the revisions of the tools used in the evaluation. Moreover, it downloads the transformation framework from git repository and sets it to the right version and branch. Further, it contains benchmarking definitions used by BenchExec to execute the experiments and processing scripts of the results that were used to generate the tables. Folder figures-generation/results-FSE2025 contains all the data that we computed.

Contents

The artifact contains the following items: - README.{html,md}: this documentation - Makefile: makefile containing all the commands for getting the source code of all the tools and our framework - benchmark-defs/: definitions needed for BenchExec to run the experiments - figures-generation/: folder containing all the processing scripts for the results and the results form our experiments - tasks/: definitions for our selected subsets of tasks that can be used to run the tool

TL;DR

  1. Setup variables in your shell environment to one of these:
    • If you have access to a BenchCloud instance use source benchmark-utils/config_vcloud.sh, adapting it correspondingly to your server
    • To execute on your local system use source benchmark-utils/config.sh. You may want to adapt the amount of processes running in parallel by adjusting the number of processes in -N 2.
  2. Select the tasks which you would like to use:
    • make tasks-benchmark: to setup all tasks used in the experiments in the paper
    • make tasks-subset: to setup tasks to run a representative subset of tasks for the experiments in the paper
    • make tasks-test: to setup a few tasks to test the functionality of the artifact
  3. If not executing inside the artifact VM, you need to install everything using make setup-all. This may take a while and you may want to set a symlink to your SV-Benchmarks copy if available.
  4. If you wish to only get the code of the transformation framework, run make specification-transformation.
  5. Execute the verification tasks on the original properties using make experiments-original-property
  6. Transform the properties to reachability using make transform-all-properties
  7. Execute the verification tasks where the original property has been encoded as a reachability property using make experiments-transformed
  8. Analyze the results to get the tables and plots from the paper using make process-results

Running BenchExec

When running BenchExec some directories need to be given as overlay, hidden and full access. Which ones are what is given in config.sh. If not using the artifact VM, you should adjust them to your own paths.

metadata.description:
This artifact is a reproduction package for the article “A Large-Scale Study on Developer Engagement and Expertise in Configurable Software System Projects”, submitted at FSE 2025. It is archived on Zenodo with the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13755747.

The FSE article investigates the expertise and engagement of developers in variable code during the evolution of CSS projects. Additionally, we study, in the FSE article, the concentration of workload for developers working on variable code. Finally, we explore the effectiveness of expertise metrics in identifying developers with high variable code engagement. The artifact, proposed in the FSE article, supports the reproduction of the experiments, with implementations of DOA and Ownership.

The artifact consists of source code and input data used in the evaluation of the study, as well as the results produced from the experiments. Specifically, it includes the source code of DOAV, which implements the algorithms utilized in the article.
